page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-8 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance powered by the Ampere Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapping to 8 physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The instance is configured with 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top tier. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is strong at 198.51 GB/sec, while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 984.48 GB/sec. Single-threaded performance is strong in compression tasks, with gzip compression at 32.3 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.14 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is weak, as shown by the PassMark CPU encryption test score of 1665.96, which is attributed to the lack of specialized hardware acceleration flags beyond basic AES support.

The c4a-standard-8 is designed for general-purpose workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth without requiring x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX. It is well-suited for static web serving, database operations, and Redis caching, where it achieves 17.51 million operations per second. The Arm-based architecture offers a cost-efficient profile by delivering competitive resource density and strong memory performance relative to its hardware class, making it a viable option for multi-threaded applications, microservices, and lightweight language model inference.
